why_structural_not_another_condition: Rounds 1-3 each bounded the predicate by enumerating what to refuse and each list was incomplete -- the shape that took #259/#260 through three rejections. A fourth condition would not have converged. Unlike that problem this one is BOUNDED: a GitHub-markdown table has a defined shape, so the predicate asserts the shape and returns False for everything else. Every exit in _grid_starts_at is False; the only True is the end.

shape.rows[i+1]: separator, N cells, EVERY cell matching :?-{3,}:?
shape.rows[i+2:]: body, at least one CONTENT row -- N cells, not blank, and not itself a separator

structural_predicate.separator_position: i+1 specifically, never merely 'somewhere' in the block
structural_predicate.body_position: strictly from i+2, so a separator can never be counted as the body row after itself
structural_predicate.offset_rationale: A run may open with pipe-bearing prose above the real table. Each candidate offset must satisfy the WHOLE shape, so this is not laxity; it keeps a genuine grid from being lost to a stray sentence above it.
structural_predicate.fence_awareness: _strip_fenced_regions runs FIRST and blanks fenced content AND the fence lines, so a grid opening immediately after a fence with no blank line cannot inherit the fence's row. Only a fence of the same character (` or ~) closes one. An UNCLOSED fence swallows the rest of the document on purpose: the document is malformed and this predicate suppresses a fail-closed marker, so the honest answer under malformation is 'no grid here'.
structural_predicate.default: False -- a case nobody anticipated fails closed, pinned by test_the_predicate_fails_closed_on_a_shape_nobody_enumerated

fourth_phantom_found_by_self_testing.why_the_first_structural_attempt_missed_: The body check required 'at least one non-empty cell', and a separator cell (---) IS non-empty text.
fourth_phantom_found_by_self_testing.structural_remedy: A body row must be CONTENT: right width, not blank, AND not itself a separator. Structure is not a reading.
fourth_phantom_found_by_self_testing.note: Found by running the enumeration, not by re-reading the diff.
